item.title: DECwindows Motif
item.description:
Development Tools DECwindows Motif Jump to Section Jump to Section Product Overview A GUI to an OpenVMS system. With DECwindows Motif, as in all X Window System environments, the server system resides on the desktop and displays graphics onscreen. 8-2 Features The following components make up the DECwindows Motif client software:Desktop applicationsX Window System utilitiesSession management utilitiesProgramming libraries: X Library (Xlib), X Toolkit Intrinsics (Xt), OSF/Motif toolkit (Xm), VSI Extensions to Motif (DXm), Inter-Client Exchange (ICE), and X Session Management (XSMP) Extensions Documentation Documents and manuals related to this product Using DECwindows Motif for OpenVMS VSI DECwindows Motif for OpenVMS Installation Guide VSI DECwindows Motif for OpenVMS Management Guide VSI DECwindows Motif for OpenVMS Guide to Application Programming Downloads Useful files related to the product, such as tools or additional materials.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 4 Comments:

flomo:

I dunno what's interesting about this link, but Motif has been LGPL a while and the last release was in 2017.

https://sourceforge.net/projects/motif/files/

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motif_%28software%29

(in some alternate universe, motif was under the x11 license and you would have motif v13 instead of GTK.)

jmward01:

I saw DEC windows and immediately thought of Windows NT 3.1.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_NT_3.1

tokyobreakfast:

I miss Motif. This is a portal to a time when men were men and UNIX(R)—or in this case, VMS—desktops were utilitarian and did exactly what you needed and nothing more.

Now we live in a time where we allocate GBs of RAM to eye candy that functionally accomplishes nothing. Then we make the case to rewrite the eye candy in increasingly "safe" languages, requiring even more RAM.

hackyhacky:

item.title: Putting Gemini to Work in Chrome
item.description:
Parisa Tabriz Vice President, Chrome Share x. Gemini in Chrome now opens in a side panel, for easier multitasking. Gemini in Chrome works with other Google apps, such as Gmail.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 3 Comments:

firefoxd:

I must be using web browsers completely wrong. Like browsing a page isn't a problem for me. I can do it at the speed of my needs.

I'm having a hard time understanding why I will tell gemini to create an account on some website for me or send an email. Those are usually just a tab away. That's why I feel like I'm missing something here.

hackyhacky:

Serious question, not snark: Does anyone actually want this? I honestly can't imagine a use for these features even among people tech savvy enough to understand them.

ukuina:

This is a big deal, the highlight is Chrome autobrowse. Goes head-to-head with OpenAI Atlas.
